evidence.quote: #### Organization, inputs and uniformity Section 1 gives the analytic reduction and the precise packet estimates needed for the band theorem.

requires_concepts: finite Fourier inequality with constant one

outputs.exact_statement:
Let $v:\mathbb R^2\to S^1$ be Lipschitz and $0<\delta<1$. Restrict to rectangles satisfying $$L(R)\le \frac1{100\mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(v)},\qquad
 \left|R\cap v^{-1}(\operatorname{EX}(R))\right|\ge\delta\left|R\right|,$$ where the first restriction is void when $\mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(v)=0$. Then $$\mathcal M_{v,\delta}h(z)
   =\sup_R\frac{\mathbf 1_R(z)}{\left|R\right|}\int_R\left|h\right|
 \quad\text{satisfies}\quad
 \left\|\mathcal M_{v,\delta}h\right\|_{L^{2,\infty}}
       \le C\delta^{-1/2}\left\|h\right\|_2.$$ Here the supremum is tested at every point of $R$, and the constant is independent of $v$ and $\delta$.
The uniform restricted estimate in [thm:band-restricted](#thm:band-restricted) implies [thm:main](#thm:main).

For any fixed $1<p<\infty$, the contribution of $\max(\epsilon,\tau)<|t|<a$ to $HP_w$ has $L^p$ norm at most $C_p(1+L)$ if $L\ge L_0$, and at most a fixed $C_p$ otherwise. On the remaining times below $w$, replacing $u$ by zero costs a uniformly bounded $L^p$ operator. The resulting horizontal symmetric truncation is uniformly bounded on $L^p$.

Let $h:\mathbb R^2\to\mathcal H$ satisfy $$\left\|h\right\|_\infty\le Q,\qquad
 \left\|h\right\|_1\le Q M_0,\qquad
 \left\|h\right\|_2^2\le C_0M_0,$$ where $M_0>0$ and $Q\le C\exp(C L^{0.9})$. Write $$A_i=\{2^{i-1}<\left\|h(\cdot)\right\|_{\mathcal H}\le2^i\},
 \qquad a_i=2^i\sqrt{|A_i|/M_0}.$$ For sufficiently large absolute $L$, $$\label{red:level-weight-bounds}
 \sum_i a_i\le C\sqrt{1+L},\qquad
 \sum_{\{i:\,|\log(|A_i|/M_0)|>L/4\}}a_i
       \le C e^{-cL}.$$ Empty level sets are omitted. The constants depend on the fixed constants in the hypotheses, not on the dimension of $\mathcal H$.

The diagonal form $$\sum_j\langle\mathcal A_{u,\mathcal L} \widetilde Q_j f_j,g_j\rangle$$ is a sum, with absolutely summable scalar coefficients, of averages of forms [eq:src-3]. Each form satisfies [red:packets](#red:packets), uniformly in $w,m,\mathcal L$, and has one common angular grid and common spatial lattices across components. The same assertion holds for $m=1$ with the original positive-frequency band cutoff in place of $\widetilde Q_1$. The sums can be obtained as limits of finite packet collections.

Suppose that the following bounds hold, uniformly for every admissible finite form $\Lambda_{\mathcal S}$ in [red:packets](#red:packets), with the fixed packet constants there. The field $u:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R$ is bounded and measurable, the sets $F,E\subset\mathbb R^2$ are measurable with positive finite measure, and the input and test satisfy $\left\|f(z)\right\|_{\mathcal H}\le\mathbf 1_F(z)$, $\left\|g(z)\right\|_{\mathcal H}\le\mathbf 1_E(z)$.* 1. *For $m\ge1$, there is a fixed exponent $C_1$ such that $$\label{red:model-basic} |\Lambda_{\mathcal S}(f,g)| \le C(1+\log(2m))^{C_1}\sqrt{|F||E|}.$$* 2. *For $L\ge L_0$, with $\tau,m,W$ as in [red:small-time-parameters], assume in addition that $\left|u\right|\le1$, $\mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(u)\le C_{\rm Lip}$, and $F,E\subset I\times\mathbb R$ for an interval $I$ with $\left|I\right|\le b_0$. Whenever $L/2\le\log\sqrt{|E|/|F|}\le2L$, $$\label{red:model-improved} |\Lambda_{\mathcal S}(f,g)| \le C L^{-20}\sqrt{|F||E|}.$$* 3. *For $m=1$, one scalar component, and $|E|\le|F|$, there is a fixed $c>0$ such that $$\label{red:model-reverse} |\Lambda_{\mathcal S}(f,g)| \le C\sqrt{|F||E|}(|E|/|F|)^c.$$* *Then holds. The constants remain uniform in $w$, $\epsilon$, and the number of retained scales.

Suppose $\operatorname{size}(v)\leq C_*\sigma$, with $C_*$ fixed. One can remove a collection of trees so that the remaining size is at most $\sigma$ and $$\label{tile:eq-size-budget} \sum_T|R_T|\leq C\sigma^{-2}\left\|f\right\|_2^2.$$ The removed tiles partition into ordinary trees satisfying [tile:eq-tree]; their total top area has the same bound.

For $0<\eta\leq C$, all tiles with $D_E(s)>\eta$ can be assigned to keeper boxes $R_T$, of dyadic length $l_T\leq\tau$, width $W$, and slope $t_T$, with the following properties. There are pairwise disjoint measurable sets $E_T$ such that $$\begin{gathered}
 E_T\subset E\cap K_\eta R_T
                 \cap\{u\in\Omega(t_T,l_T)\},\qquad
 |E_T|\geq c\eta|R_T|,
                  \label{tile:eq-density-witnesses}\\
 \sum_T|R_T|\leq C\eta^{-1}|E|,\qquad
 K_\eta\leq C(1+\eta^{-1/100}),
                  \label{tile:eq-keeper-budget}\\
 \ell_s\leq l_T,\qquad t_T\in\Omega_s,\qquad
 z_s\in C K_\eta R_T
 \quad\text{for each tile assigned to }T.
                  \label{tile:eq-density-assignment}
\end{gathered}$$ After partitioning by centers, the assigned tiles form ordinary test trees of total top area at most $$\label{tile:eq-density-budget}
 C\eta^{-1}(1+\eta^{-1/20})|E|.$$

The mask has Fourier support $$\label{forest:eq-mask-spectrum}
 \mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\widehat q_T\subset
 \left\{(\xi,\eta):
       |\xi+s_T\eta|\le\frac{r_L}{L^A l_T},\quad
       |\eta|\le\frac{r_L}{L^A W}\right\}.$$ For sufficiently large $L$, with all other exponents fixed, $$\begin{aligned}
 |q_T(z)|&\le \exp(-L\log L)
       &&\text{if }\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_T(z)>K_0,
       \label{forest:eq-mask-outside}\\
 |q_T(z)|h_T(z)^{-1}&\le C
       &&\text{for all }z,
       \label{forest:eq-mask-weight}\\
 |1-q_T(z)|&\le C L^{1-A}
       &&\text{if }\mathop{\mathrm{dist}}_T(z)\le L^{A/2}.
       \label{forest:eq-mask-inside}
\end{aligned}$$ In particular multiplication by $q_T$ adds at most $O(L^{1-A})$ times the bandwidths of the top box to a Fourier support.

Let $I$ be a finite interval and let $f$ be a locally integrable scalar function on $I$. Suppose that for each dyadic subinterval $J$ of $I$, $\left|J\right|^{-1}\int_J\left|f-f_J\right|\leq A$, where $f_J$ denotes its average. Then, for every $b\geq1$, $$\left(\frac1{\left|I\right|}\int_I\left|f\right|^b\right)^{1/b}
 \leq\left|f_I\right|+CbA.$$

For every slope $t$, every collection satisfying [eq:src-9], every line $Y_t=y_0$, every horizontal interval $I$ of length $l$ on that line, and every $b\geq2$, the normalized $L^b(I)$ norms of $\mathcal E_t$, $\mathcal S_t$, and $$\mathcal V_3\left(\sum_{\ell_s=2^k}\phi_s\right), \qquad \mathcal V_3\left(\sum_{\ell_s=2^k}q_{T(s)}\phi_s\right)$$ are at most $C b^C(1+\log B)^C$. The constants are uniform in the line, interval, finite collection, dimension, and number of scales. In particular the assertion holds for every fixed deterministic subcollection with the same constants.

Let $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_d\in\mathbb R$, where $d\le D$, satisfy $\left|\lambda_i-\lambda_j\right|\ge\Delta>0$ for $i\ne j$. Let $\nu$ be any positive probability measure on $\mathbb R$ such that $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\widehat\nu\subset(-\epsilon_0\Delta,\epsilon_0\Delta)$. Then, for every finite $p\ge4$ and every complex coefficient sequence, $$\left(\int_\mathbb R
       \left|\sum_{i=1}^d a_i e^{i\lambda_i t}\right|^p
       \,\,\mathrm d\nu(t)\right)^{1/p}
 \le \left(\sum_{i=1}^d |a_i|^{r_*}\right)^{1/r_*}.
 \label{eq:src-13}$$ The same estimate holds for coefficients in a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal H$ when the exponentials act diagonally: in an orthonormal basis, the $\xi$-th component may use frequencies $\lambda_{i,\xi}$, provided they are $\Delta$-separated as $i$ varies, for each fixed $\xi$. The right side is then $(\sum_i\left\|a_i\right\|_{\mathcal H}^{r_*})^{1/r_*}$. All these estimates have constant one.

For a separated frequency list as above, define $$\mathcal Q=\{(i,j,k,l):
    |\lambda_i+\lambda_j-\lambda_k-\lambda_l|
       <\epsilon_0\Delta\}.$$ Let $x_i\ge0$, $\sum_i x_i=1$, and put $$Q(x)=\sum_{(i,j,k,l)\in\mathcal Q}
                (x_i x_j x_k x_l)^{3/4}.$$ Then $Q(x)\le1$. If $0<\kappa<1$ and $\max_i x_i\le1-\kappa$, then $$Q(x)\le1-\delta_\kappa,
 \qquad
 \delta_\kappa=
       \frac{\kappa^4(1-\kappa/2)^2}{4096}
       \ge 2^{-14}\kappa^4.
 \label{phase:quantitative-gap}$$

Fix an eligible path from a root $v_0(T)$ through level $k$. At every spatial point, $$\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}R_i
 \le K\log\frac{n_{v_0(T)}}{n_{v_k(T)}},
 \qquad
 \sum_{i=0}^{k-1}P_i
 =\log\frac{n_{v_0(T)}}{n_{v_k(T)}}.
 \label{hier:full-root-telescope}$$ For a fixed starting level $h\le k_T$, define, for $h\le k\le k_T$, $$\omega_{T,h,k}(\zeta,z)
 =n_{v_k(T)}(z)^{-\mu/K}
   \prod_{i=h}^{k-1}w_{v_{i+1}(T)}(\zeta,z).$$ If $0\le\Re\zeta_\sigma\le\mu$ for every $\sigma$, then the supremum plus total variation of this sequence, with the endpoint $k$ varying, is bounded by $$\sup_{h\le k\le k_T}|\omega_{T,h,k}|
 +\sum_{k=h}^{k_T-1}
       |\omega_{T,h,k+1}-\omega_{T,h,k}|
 \le C h_T^{-\mu/K}
 \left[1+K(1+\left\|\zeta\right\|_2)
                   \log\frac{n_{v_0(T)}}{h_T}\right].
 \label{eq:src-16}$$ The same bound holds upon restricting the endpoints to a subinterval.

Fix $R,J,j$ as above and an interval $I$ of horizontal length $H_j$ on a line of slope $s_R$. Consider the masses $n_J,n_c,m_c$ in [eq:src-18], the masses used in the factors $\lambda_c$, and those used in any endpoint multiplier of a packet contributing to $A_c$. Each such mass, and each of its positive subset-complement differences used below, is a sum of weights of tops $T$ satisfying $$|s_T-s_R|\le C\rho_j, \qquad d_T\le\rho_j/B^2. \label{hier:motion-locality}$$ There is an absolute constant $C$ such that, with $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mov}}=C G^{-1/2}$, every nonzero such mass $a$ satisfies $$|\partial_x\log a|\le\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mov}}}{H_j} \quad\text{almost everywhere on }I. \label{hier:mass-log-derivative}$$ If $r=a/(a+b)$ is one of the ratios of a submass to its containing mass, then $$|\partial_x\log r| \le\frac{2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mov}}}{H_j}(1-r) \le\frac{2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mov}}}{H_j}(-\log r). \label{hier:ratio-derivative}$$ When $b=0$, the ratio is identically one and its derivative is zero. In particular, nonzero $n_J-n_c$ and $m_c-n_c$ have the relative motion bound [hier:mass-log-derivative]. All these masses vary by a factor $1+O(G^{-1/2})$ across $I$.* *For the parameters [hier:vertex-parameters], the block factors also satisfy, for $x,x_0\in I$, $$\left|\frac{\lambda_c(x)}{\lambda_c(x_0)}-1\right| \le G^{-c_0} \label{hier:complex-transition-motion}$$ for some absolute $c_0>0$ and all sufficiently large $L$.

There is a fixed exponent $C_{\mathrm{path}}$, chosen independently of the mass cutoff below, such that the following construction is valid. Call $R$ bad at $z$ if any of $\mathcal E_R(z),\mathcal S_R(z),\mathcal V_{R,\sigma}(z)$, $0\le\sigma[eq:src-7], using the original adjoint sum’s $L^2$ bound.

Fix $z\in Z$, a root, a shift, and parameters as above. Starting from a node with $n_J>M$, expand $$V_J=\beta_J \left(n_J-\sum_c n_c+\sum_c V_c\right), \label{hier:exact-expansion}$$ and stop a branch on first reaching a node of mass at most $M$. At each expanding node, split $n_J-\sum_c n_c$ into the individual weights of the tops which do not remain eligible at the block endpoint. At a stopped node split $V_J$ proportionally among its eligible top weights. This gives exactly one terminal path for each eligible root top $R$, with a terminal amount $e_R$ satisfying $$0M$, at least one half of this sum comes from tops which are good at $z$. Consequently, $$V_{\mathrm{root}}(z) \le 2C_M\sum_{\substack{R\text{ eligible at root}\\R\text{ good at }z}} h_R(z)\prod_{J\text{ active on }R\text{'s path}}\beta_J(z). \label{hier:good-path-domination}$$ If $n_{\mathrm{root}}\le M$, [hier:small-node-amount] applies instead.

At a point of $Z_0$, the active path drops satisfy $$\sum_{j:\,n_j>M}u_j
 \le 1+\log^+\frac{n_0}{M}\le C L.
 \label{hier:drop-budget}$$ On each line of slope $s_R$, mark an $H_j$ cell $I$ when $$\inf_{z\in I}n_j(z)>M,
 \qquad
 \sup_{z\in I}h_j^*(z)\ge\frac12.
 \label{eq:src-23}$$ Every point of a marked cell is active and has $h_j^*\ge c$ for an absolute $c>0$. At an active point in an unmarked cell with $h_j^*\ge1$, one has $M<n_j<M+1$ for all sufficiently large $L$. There is at most one such index on each active path, and its factor is bounded at points of $Z_0$ by $$\beta_{J_j}\le L^{Cp}(1+M)^C.
 \label{hier:missing-factor}$$ If an index is inactive at a point, the cell containing that point is unmarked. Finally, even in the last possible block, $$H_j\le\frac{l_R}{B\sqrt G}.
 \label{hier:mesh-within-top}$$

There is an absolute $c_{\rm av}>0$ with the following property, for all sufficiently large $L$. On a fixed line of slope $s_R$, each marked $H_j$-cell $I$ meeting $Z$ admits a nonnegative function $\Gamma_j$ which is constant on the $H_{j-1}$-subcells of $I$, satisfies $|I|^{-1}\int_I\Gamma_j\le1$, and obeys $$\beta_J^0(z)\le
       \exp\bigl(G^{-c_{\rm av}}u_j(z)\bigr)\Gamma_j(z)
       \qquad (z\in I).
 \label{eq:src-24}$$ Set $\Gamma_j=1$ on unmarked cells and on cells not meeting $Z$. The functions can be chosen measurably on each fixed line. No choice jointly measurable in the family of parallel lines is needed.

There is a fixed sufficiently small $\epsilon'>0$ such that, with $$Q=G^{3/4}ho_{j+1},\qquad \delta=\epsilon' Q/w,
 \label{pred:separation-bandwidth}$$ every positive probability $
u$ satisfying $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\widehat
u\subset(-\delta,\delta)$ obeys $\int\widetilde eta\,\,\mathrm d
u\le1$.

At a point $z\in Z$ where $R$ is a good path, $$\left(\sum_j\left\|B_{J_j}(z)\right\|^2\right)^{1/2}\le L^{C_b}.
  \label{res:block-square-bound}$$ Here the sum can be restricted to any subset of the possible blocks. The fixed exponent $C_b$ is independent of $M$.

Uniformly over the segments and their starting indices, $$\sup_{i_j\le k<i_f}|\omega_j(k)|
    +\sum_{k=i_j}^{i_f-2}|\omega_j(k+1)-\omega_j(k)|
       \le L^{C_w}.
  \label{res:common-weight-BV}$$ The exponent $C_w$ is fixed before $M$ is chosen.

With $M$ chosen by [res:choice-M], the estimate [eq:src-22] holds for every path top $R$, every shift, and every vertex parameter with $\left\|\Im\zeta\right\|_2\le L^2$. Its constants are independent of the tile collection, angular depth, and Hilbert-space dimension.
Equation [eq:src-29] also holds at $$\zeta^{\mathrm c}=(\mu/K,\ldots,\mu/K).$$
The popular adjoint sum satisfies Equation [eq:src-7]; namely, $$\int_F\|P\|\lesssim L^{-20}N|F|.$$

For the packet forms in [eq:src-3], let $u$ be a bounded measurable real slope, let $F,E\subset\mathbb R^2$ be measurable sets of positive finite measure, and suppose $\|f\|_{\mathcal H}\le\mathbf 1_F$ and $\|g\|_{\mathcal H}\le\mathbf 1_E$ pointwise. The following estimates hold uniformly over every finite subcollection.* 1. *For $m\ge1$, $$|\Lambda(f,g)|\lesssim(1+\log(2m))^C\sqrt{|F||E|}.$$* 2. *Suppose $L\ge L_0$, with $\tau,m,W$ chosen by [red:small-time-parameters], and $L/2\le\log\sqrt{|E|/|F|}\le2L$. If $\left|u\right|\le1$, $\mathop{\mathrm{Lip}}(u)\le C_{\rm Lip}$, and $F,E\subset I\times\mathbb R$ for an interval $I$ of length at most $b_0$, then $$|\Lambda(f,g)|\lesssim L^{-20}\sqrt{|F||E|}.$$* 3. *For the scalar model with $m=1$ and $|E|\le|F|$, there is an absolute $c>0$ such that $$|\Lambda(f,g)|\lesssim \sqrt{|F||E|}\left(\frac{|E|}{|F|}\right)^c.$$
